source.title: On the distance between two neural networks and the stability of learning
source.authors: Jeremy Bernstein; Arash Vahdat; Yisong Yue; Ming-Yu Liu

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training outcomes, but none of its measurements tests the specific training-error, shortcut, initialization, learning-rate-stability, or batch-normalization claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports benchmark training losses and MLP training-accuracy results. These are relevant to training behavior, but the text does not report the classification-error outcomes named in V1, or the specific conditions and comparisons named in V2–V6. Figure 3 supplies no exact accuracy values in the text.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates an optimizer and parameter-perturbation geometry. It does not directly test any listed version: CIFAR-10 results report loss rather than classification error, and the depth experiments change optimizers in MNIST MLPs rather than test the architectures or initialization comparisons specified in V3–V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the depth comparison, but 'lower training error' needs clarification: the benchmarks measure classifier loss, GAN FID, and transformer perplexity. Fromage improves these training metrics over SGD on all four tasks and over Adam on three. The central conclusion is that deep relative trust motivates Fromage, whose initial learning rate of 0.01 worked across the modern benchmarks, while plain MLPs required depth-dependent learning rates. Benchmark learning rates were still decayed during training.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates Fromage, a layerwise relative-update optimizer, rather than the gradient-training recipes and interventions described in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: For MLPs, the authors report that deeper networks required a smaller Fromage learning rate; Figure 3 varies depth and learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-18 achieves very small CIFAR-10 training losses under SGD, Adam, and Fromage after 350 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 recipes attain near-zero training loss.

fits_no_version.finding: Fromage trains plain MNIST MLPs through at least 50 layers; the tested SGD and Adam settings fail beyond 25 layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects the trainable depth of plain ReLU MNIST MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss and relative gradient change grow quasi-exponentially with relative parameter perturbations in a 16-layer MLP, with milder breakdown at depth two.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth increases sensitivity to simultaneous layerwise relative parameter perturbations.

record.problems: The Figure 3 accuracy values are presented only in a plot, without exact values in the text. The CIFAR-10 training result reports loss, not classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results that measure a behavior named by V1–V6 were identified.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and effects of model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and the effect of adding student neurons.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized CNNs versus identity residual networks; special deep tanh initialization and Fixup.
Effects of activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and orthogonal convolution kernels on speed and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch normalization versus otherwise comparable unnormalized networks, higher learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Small classification losses are suggestive of near-zero classification error, but the supplied CIFAR-10 results do not directly establish that measure. Neither learning-rate tuning nor perturbation-induced gradient breakdown establishes V5's stability-threshold dynamics.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports CIFAR-10 training loss, not classification error or results with corrupted or random labels; it does not compare model sizes, early stopping, or the listed recipes.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or comparison of student and teacher widths.
No plain versus residual convolutional comparison, and no tests of the specified deep tanh or normalization-free residual recipes.
No comparison of initialization schemes or activation and gradient propagation across depth.
No sweep around a stability limit, curvature measurement, or reported recovery or divergence behavior at above-limit rates.
No batch-normalized versus unnormalized comparison or test of Fixup.

rows.subject: resnet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained for CIFAR-10 classification; training loss reported for SGD.
rows.uncertainty: ± 0.2, as included in the reported value
rows.note: The paper reports loss rather than training classification error.
rows.check: The reported loss is correct. It is very small, but CIFAR-10 classification error is not reported, and the supplied text does not specify this benchmark's loss sufficiently to derive an error bound. Uncertainty is ±0.2 × 10−4.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptrons
rows.operation_detail: Compared SGD, Adam, and Fromage across network depths on MNIST; training accuracy plotted after 100 epochs.
rows.note: The paper states that off-the-shelf optimizers could not train MLPs over 25 layers deep and Fromage trained up to at least depth 50; exact accuracy values are only plotted.
rows.check: This records an optimizer-by-depth comparison in plain ReLU MNIST MLPs, not a listed version. Split the aggregate row by optimizer and depth if retaining it. Each plotted optimizer result selects the best of three learning rates; the text states that SGD/Adam failed beyond 25 layers while Fromage trained through at least 50.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
